NEW YORK, Nov 12 : Retail bought the Nvidia dip on Thursday in a big way, showing the AI trade is very much alive despite CEO Jensen Huang’s departure. Nvidia was off 5 per cent on Thursday afternoon following Huang’s resignation, which followed a report on Wednesday that the founder of the second most-valuable US-listed firm had an affair with a company executive who reported to him.  Thursday’s drop put Nvidia’s market-value decline for the week at $550 billion, with selling driven initially by questions about Huang’s relationship with a woman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. But buying the dip has been favored by investors ever since the end of the financial crisis in 2009, and Thursday was no different.  “Every time it works, it gets further reinforced,” said Mark Hackett, chief market strategist at Nationwide Financial in Downingtown, Pennsylvania. “It’s the kind of idiosyncratic behavior that you get in a healthy market.”

The rebound came after Nvidia tumbled as much as 14 per cent at Thursday’s open, extending a torrent of selling over the past month. Vanda Research called Thursday's open the biggest-ever first-half-hour retail flow into Nvidia, estimated at $111 million.   "I said to somebody an hour ago in the office, this feels like the calmest day in markets in a few weeks, which is insane given the news since the last close,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St. Louis, Missouri. “I think that a lot of damage has been done to Nvidia stock over the last couple of weeks.”  Nvidia stock has lost nearly a third of its value in the five weeks since the Nasdaq Composite hit its most recent high, shedding more than $1 trillion in market value.  On Thursday, retail buyers flocked to popular investment platforms. At Fidelity Investments, customers had placed 394,818 buy orders for Nvidia by noon ET, compared with 80,088 sell orders. Buy orders for Nvidia more than doubled the combined buy orders on Thursday for the nine other most-traded stocks on the platform, with runner-up Advanced Micro Devices showing 24,790 buy orders and third-placed Nebius amassing 24,519. Sentiment was hardly unanimous. On Reddit's popular wallstreetbets trading forum, 60 per cent of comments about Nvidia were negative. A wave of Wall Street downgrades this week hasn’t helped, with analysts at Baird Equity Research on Wednesday cutting the stock to neutral and slashing their price target by 60 per cent to $200 a share, which is still far above Thursday’s afternoon price of $164. “2027 data center forecasts are being delayed due to very recent lack of visibility, with supply issues mostly the reason for a potential slowdown but also due to potential demand softening. AI hyperscaler capex could slow to 40 per cent growth or slightly less for 2027,” senior research analyst Tristan Gerra wrote.  Looking ahead, investors said the key issues for the market include what Nvidia executives say on next Tuesday’s quarterly earnings conference call and Anthropic’s IPO, which is expected to come to market later next week.  “The outlook for AI is going to be just fine,” said Hackett. He said he believes the Anthropic IPO is likely the more important event next week because, with Nvidia’s new management just having started, “It’s going to be hard for them to get a get out of jail free card out of one conference call.”

Source: Reuters

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 12 : Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter, Reuters has learned. The revelation follows two other extramarital affairs that led to his resignation Thursday. The two women are Alice Huang, who US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care.  Reuters is not naming the second employee. Attempts to reach the woman were not successful.  Nvidia declined to comment. Powell, Jensen Huang, and a representative for Nvidia's board did not reply to requests for comment. Alice Huang could not be reached for comment. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

NEW YORK, Nov 12 : Options traders cashed in parts of their bets against Nvidia and positioned for a longer-term share price recovery on Thursday, after CEO Jensen Huang announced he was stepping down. Huang's departure has raised uncertainty over the future direction of the AI chipmaker he built into one of the world's most valuable companies. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent successor. The leadership turmoil sent options volatility soaring on Thursday, but options trading suggested that investors were repositioning for a recovery rather than fleeing the stock.  "Nvida's competitive advantage and customers don't disappear overnight," said Seth Hickle, chief investment officer at Mindset Wealth Management. "The market is trying to determine whether this is a temporary leadership crisis or something that fundamentally changes the AI investment thesis."

Options give holders the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell the underlying stock at a set price before a certain date. Call options typically gain value when the stock rises, while puts gain when it falls. Several large options trades showed investors rolling bullish positions further into 2027, lowering upside targets and taking profits on downside hedges rather than abandoning exposure to the company altogether, data from Chris Murphy, co-head of derivatives strategy at Susquehanna, showed. In one trade, an investor sold put options and bought cheaper ones, collecting about $18.9 million while keeping some protection against a further drop, Murphy said. Another investor paid about $18.8 million for call spreads, a bet that pays off fully if Nvidia climbs about 16 per cent from current levels by March. Other trades pushed bullish positions out by three months and lowered the price targets, adding time for a recovery to play out. Investors also bought about 50,000 January call options, spending an estimated $45.3 million to $55 million to bet the shares will rise above current levels by expiry. Nvidia's shares were last down 4.84 per cent at $165.40. Nvidia's 90-day implied volatility has climbed to about 52 per cent from roughly 33 per cent a month ago, reflecting growing uncertainty ahead of the company's earnings report next week, according to Susquehanna data. "Implied (volatility) will remain high until the earnings report, and subsequently the conference call as it can shed some clarity about how Nvidia plans to move forward past this boondoggle," Hickle said.

Source: Reuters

NEW YORK, Nov 12 : Kalshi has ended its advisory contract with Donald Trump Jr, after his venture capital firm 1789 Capital increased its stake in arch-rival Polymarket, according to a spokesperson for the $40 billion prediction markets startup.  "We have mutually agreed to end Don's advisory role after his firm's significant investment in a competitor this past summer. We are grateful for his contributions in helping us market Kalshi to more customers," the spokesperson said, adding that the decision was mutual and the conversations to end the contract started in August since 1789 led Polymarket's most recent funding round.  Trump Jr was named a "strategic advisor" to Kalshi in January 2025 and was given a stake in the company that the Financial Times reported at the time was worth $300,000. Prediction markets first rose to prominence in 2024 as they strongly diverged from traditional opinion polls by signaling a Trump victory. Kalshi, at the time, boasted about the accuracy of its own polls, while criticizing other polls and "traditional media" for failing to anticipate Trump’s "decisive victory." Now, such platforms face the prospect of heightened scrutiny from Democrats in the US Congress. Senator Elizabeth Warren, for instance, has vowed to crack down on insider trading on prediction markets. Polymarket and Donald Trump Jr did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Source: Reuters

NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 12 : Private equity firms CD&R and GTCR have dropped their pursuit of Global Payments, according to two people familiar with the matter. The buyout consortium walked away from talks to acquire the payments processor after exploring a potential deal over the past several weeks, the people said. The talks, which were in early stages, did not advance given the complexities of arranging a take-private of this scale, prompting the firms to put their efforts on hold, the people added. The end of the discussions removes one of the largest potential leveraged buyouts in the payments sector, at a time when buyout firms are grappling with higher borrowing costs and tougher financing markets for mega-deals. It is possible that CD&R and GTCR will resume the talks with Global Payments at a later date or another buyer for the company may emerge, the people said.

Atlanta-based Global Payments, which has a market value of about $26.4 billion, is one of the world's largest payments processors, helping merchants accept card and digital payments while also providing software and technology services to businesses. The company has been under pressure in recent years from slower growth in some of its business lines, intensifying competition and investor demands to improve profitability. Global Payments has already been reshaping its portfolio. In April 2025, it agreed to acquire Worldpay from FIS and private equity firm GTCR in a transaction valued at more than $24 billion, while simultaneously agreeing to sell its issuer-solutions business to FIS. The transactions were aimed at sharpening Global Payments' focus on merchant services and expanding its scale in payment processing. A takeover of Global Payments would have ranked among the largest private equity transactions attempted this year. But arranging financing for deals of that size remains challenging, particularly amid market volatility and lenders' scrutiny of leverage levels for large buyouts. WASHINGTON, Nov 12 : The International Monetary Fund is closely monitoring volatility in AI equity valuations and the US political shift that could slow data center development, but says it is too early to tell whether investors are souring on the sector for the long term.  IMF spokesperson Julie Kozack told a regular press briefing that AI equity valuations remain exposed to a reassessment of the longer-term profitability of the technology. "That overall view that we have taken still remains the case," she said. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sent the company's shares sharply lower on Thursday, dragging down the S&P 500 and Nasdaq indexes, but some major tech stocks rose, including Nvidia rival Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet and Microsoft.  Asked about the impact on the AI sector from the stock gyrations, as well as pledges by newly elected Democratic governors to slow data center development, Kozack said: "We're of course are closely monitoring the most recent developments and their impact on equity markets, the economy, and financial stability, but at this point it's really too early to say whether there's going to be some broader reassessment of investment in AI technology and any broader reassessment of profitability and future productivity gains."

NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 12 : US stocks reversed early losses to trade slightly higher on Thursday even as Nvidia shares fell following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. The 10-year US Treasury yield climbed back above 5 per cent. Nvidia said Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO as the company looks for a permanent successor. Nvidia shares were last down about 4 per cent but off the day's lows. Huang's resignation raises questions about the chipmaker's future and the AI boom. The move follows news Huang had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. Shares of competitor Advanced Micro Devices were up 7 per cent. Broadcom rose 5.4 per cent, while Intel was flat.

Some investors are concerned Washington may curb access to offshore data centers with the most advanced processors. INDEXES UP SLIGHTLY The three major US stock indexes, however, edged higher, with an index of semiconductors up 0.2 per cent after reversing early declines. A world stocks index was flat. "The market's absorbed this reasonably well. You notice some of Nvidia's losses have been offset by gains in competitors," said Peter Tuz, president of Chase Investment Counsel in Charlottesville, Virginia. "As far as Nvidia's future, there's a lot that remains unknown about this whole episode," he said. "Are we seeing the bottom today? Will there be more bad news coming out that will drive down the stock again? That's the existential question looking at Nvidia today. " The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 210.10 points, or 0.40 per cent, to 52,696.65, the S&P 500 gained 21.99 points, or 0.29 per cent, to 7,641.10 and the Nasdaq Composite added 79.16 points, or 0.31 per cent, to 25,545.34. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe eased 0.02 points to 1,121.13. The pan-European STOXX 600 index was last up 0.23 per cent. It hit its first record high since August. US Treasury yields rose after US President Donald Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 7.73 basis points to 5.066 per cent.  Germany's 10-year Bund yield dipped. DOLLAR EXTENDS RECENT GAINS The US dollar index reached a fresh 19-month high as investors continued to weigh US rate increase expectations. Traders see a December hike from the Federal Reserve as likely. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro,rose 0.26 per cent to 103.14, with the euro down 0.25 per cent at $1.1061. Against the Japanese yen, the dollar strengthened 0.08 per cent to 159.9. US crude rose 0.32 per cent to $86.81 a barrel and Brent climbed to $93.82 per barrel, up 1.14 per cent.

Nov 12 : SpaceX said on Thursday it plans to invest more than $74 billion in two supercomputing campuses, its Starbase site in Texas and in Cochise County, Arizona, expanding its AI computing ambitions alongside rocket and satellite businesses. The AI segment of the Elon Musk-led company, which went public in June, generated more than half of its revenue in the third quarter, highlighting how far the business has moved beyond rockets and Starlink satellite internet. SpaceX expects to spend more than $24 billion on the Starbase site and roughly $50 billion on the Arizona campus, it said in a statement. The Arizona campus, which needs approval from Cochise County, would create about 5,500 construction jobs and 1,000 permanent jobs.

"NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple," Trump said on social media. HYDERABAD, Nov 12 : US retailer Costco sees room to expand its technology presence in India beyond Hyderabad as it accelerates international growth, with its first global capability centre playing a key role in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, a top executive said. The Hyderabad centre, which employs more than 70 people, supports global operations and is expected to grow to several hundred staff over the next five to six years, Javier Polit, Costco's chief information and digital officer, told Reuters on Thursday. He did not give a specific hiring target. "We're going to grow our business internationally at a greater velocity than we have been in the past. So there'll be more presence in this geography for sure," Polit said, adding that India was already playing a key role in the retailer's growth plans.  AI has delivered productivity gains of up to 60 per cent in some technology projects, Polit said, prompting Costco to build more tools in India for global deployment, including a Hyderabad-developed geofencing tool that identifies customers approaching stores to speed check-in and checkout.

NEW YORK, Nov 12 : Warby Parker is entering the smart glasses market in partnership with Google and Samsung, betting that demand for the artificial intelligence wearables will balloon in the coming years. But the New York-based fashion brand, known for its affordable eyewear, is also seeking to head off privacy concerns that have weighed on existing producers of the glasses, most of which embed small cameras allowing wearers to record their surroundings without taking out their phone. The Warby Parker glasses are broadly similar to Meta smart glasses already available from Ray-Ban and Oakley maker EssilorLuxottica, which have faced regulatory scrutiny from Norway to Australia. Also like the Meta glasses, they will connect to an AI assistant, in this case Google's Gemini, for everything from directions to language translation.   The big difference from existing versions on the market is the privacy framework embedded in the glasses from the outset, Warby Parker Co-CEO Neil Blumenthal told Reuters.

Alphabet's Google will not use visuals captured with the glasses to train its AI. The glasses will bar facial recognition of bystanders. And a small white notification light on the front of the glasses automatically turns on when a user starts recording video. Shoppers will start placing pre-orders from Warby Parker on Thursday. Ray-Ban's Meta glasses still dominate, representing 81.3 per cent of AI glasses shipments in the first half of this year, according to tech research group Omdia. But brands from Warby Parker to luxury group Kering — poised to release glasses also in partnership with Google — are looking to gain a foothold. Global AI glasses shipments more than doubled in the first half of 2026 from a year ago, though growth has slowed since the second half of last year, Omdia data shows. Meta's AI glasses also include a camera notification light on the front, a Meta spokesperson said, adding that input from safety experts helped inform the privacy features on its glasses. CATEGORY CONFRONTS PRIVACY RISKS Optimism that Warby Parker's "intelligent eyewear" plan will prove to be a major growth engine has helped its shares rally by nearly 40 per cent this year, outperforming a 10 per cent gain in the S&P 500. The company expects an addition of several percentage points to fourth-quarter revenue growth from the new wearable technology, executives said on an earnings call earlier this month. "As long as the tools provide utility to customers, then we'll be successful," Blumenthal said. While the core optical backdrop remains soft, smart glasses are poised to be an "increasingly important driver" of Warby Parker's growth outlook, analysts at TD Cowen wrote in a research note last week.  Still, concerns about privacy could slow their pace of growth. One of Britain's biggest pub chains has restricted the use of the frames, Norway's government is planning a temporary ban on the use of AI glasses in certain locations, and Australia is considering barring the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in government workplaces. GOOGLE AIMS TO REBUILD TRUST Juston Payne, who leads extended reality products at Google, acknowledged that public skepticism could be a risk to growth. "This is an area where, understandably, trust was lost," he told Reuters at a demo for the Warby Parker glasses in New York. Google says it will embed extensive privacy guardrails into the devices to prevent tampering with the recording indicator light; redact people's faces from video footage before it is sent to Gemini; and ban targeted advertising on the glasses. "We are going to change this conversation," Payne said. "We are trying to raise the bar." But it remains to be seen whether those measures will ease concern about widespread surveillance, if the glasses become ubiquitous. "I'm certainly happy to hear that (video footage is) not automatically fed into AI systems for training," said Calli Schroeder, who leads the AI and human rights program at the Electronic Privacy Information Center, an advocacy group. "But that still leaves open: a stranger has footage of my kid on their phone. That's concerning no matter how you phrase it."

Source: Reuters

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday (Nov 12) after revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll. Huang's exit caps a tumultuous week for Nvidia , one of the major engines behind the AI boom, and could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader AI ecosystem, given the ex-CEO's push to preserve access to the Chinese market, as well as his close ties with US President Donald Trump. The crisis has threatened to implicate some Trump administration members, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is facing growing questions over the administration's oversight of chip sales to China, particularly as both he and Huang pushed for relaxing those sales despite scrutiny from longtime China hawks in both parties. The Commerce Department did not immediately comment. Senior White House officials are discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation told Reuters on Thursday.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Lutnick's future. Earlier in the day, a White House official said US President Donald Trump "maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position." Huang's departure threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped shape by pouring Nvidia 's swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry's biggest labs. The surge in AI computing demand drove a sevenfold increase in Nvidia 's shares through early October, pushing its market value at one point to nearly $6 trillion. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, considering both internal and external candidates, the company said on Thursday.

Related:

Who would be next CEO at Nvidia? Top engineer and CFO favoured as candidates

Jensen Huang scandal could spur tighter US scrutiny of AI cloud providers in Southeast Asia: Analysts

The departure has also ignited speculation over who will ultimately lead the company, long associated with the leather-jacket-wearing Huang, who co-founded Nvidia more than three decades ago. Kress and longtime Nvidia engineer Ian Buck had emerged as the leading internal candidates among investors and analysts even before Huang's departure. Nvidia shares were down about 4.8 per cent, paring earlier losses. Shares of rivals AMD and Broadcom rose about 6 per cent each. Huang, Nvidia 's fourth-largest shareholder with a 3.61 per cent stake, will also leave the board. Nvidia named former Synopsys CEO and longtime director Harvey Jones as its first board chair. "The Board, Estaff (executive staff) and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period," Kress wrote in a memo to employees, adding that the company will host a meeting on Nov 18. Kress was gathering Nvidia 's executive team at its headquarters on Thursday, CNBC reported, adding that Huang had agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving. Huang has hired law firm Paul Weiss, the New York Times reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. It was not clear what the firm had been retained to do, the report said. The company has not commented beyond its statement announcing Huang's resignation. REPLACING HUANG Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. The New York Times also reported Wednesday that Huang had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him. While Kress offers investors a familiar hand after 13 years as CFO, analysts have pointed to Buck as a potential longer-term candidate because of Nvidia 's reliance on technical leadership. The veteran engineer helped develop its crucial CUDA software platform and now leads its hyperscale AI products. "The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap ... that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system," said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments. "In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself." Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.

TRUMP WEIGHS IN Trump said on Sunday that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country" and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy. On Thursday, the US president suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over as Nvidia 's CEO. US House Speaker Mike Johnson said it was "critically important for right successor to be chosen to replace Huang," noting there was a growing consensus in Congress on limiting exports of semiconductor chips to China. HUANG'S ROCK-STAR STATUS For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips' ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world's most valuable company. That turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. The scandal preceding Huang's departure unfolded over more than a year, beginning with an October 2025 New York Times report linking him to Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips. Subsequent reports said US intelligence officials believed Alice Huang was acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy. Washington has also investigated Megaspeed over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports.

Related:

Alice Huang barred from re-entering Singapore; insufficient evidence she committed offences in Megaspeed probe: MHA

What we know about Megaspeed, Singapore-based customer of Nvidia

Separately, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday that the US Justice Department was investigating Alice Huang over whether entities linked to her were involved in efforts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products to China, citing a person familiar with the matter. A spokesperson for the Manhattan US Attorney’s office declined to comment on the Bloomberg report. The office previously charged three people associated with Super Micro, including its co-founder, with helping smuggle at least US$2.5 billion of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws. Super Micro did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Earlier, the Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs said Singapore police had been investigating Super Micro as part of a wider probe into Megaspeed and Alice Huang. The police had reached out to the FBI and the Justice Department for help and had received "limited information or assistance," the ministry said. Earlier this month, Nvidia 's board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time. The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia 's vice president of healthcare, who reported to him.

Source: Reuters/sz/fs

Huang's departure threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped shape by pouring Nvidia 's swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry's biggest labs. The surge in AI computing demand drove a sevenfold increase in Nvidia 's shares through early October, pushing its market value at one point to nearly $6 trillion. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, considering both internal and external candidates, the company said on Thursday.

Related:

Who would be next CEO at Nvidia? Top engineer and CFO favoured as candidates

Jensen Huang scandal could spur tighter US scrutiny of AI cloud providers in Southeast Asia: Analysts

The departure has also ignited speculation over who will ultimately lead the company, long associated with the leather-jacket-wearing Huang, who co-founded Nvidia more than three decades ago. Kress and longtime Nvidia engineer Ian Buck had emerged as the leading internal candidates among investors and analysts even before Huang's departure. Nvidia shares were down about 4.8 per cent, paring earlier losses. Shares of rivals AMD and Broadcom rose about 6 per cent each. Huang, Nvidia 's fourth-largest shareholder with a 3.61 per cent stake, will also leave the board. Nvidia named former Synopsys CEO and longtime director Harvey Jones as its first board chair. "The Board, Estaff (executive staff) and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period," Kress wrote in a memo to employees, adding that the company will host a meeting on Nov 18. Kress was gathering Nvidia 's executive team at its headquarters on Thursday, CNBC reported, adding that Huang had agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving. Huang has hired law firm Paul Weiss, the New York Times reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. It was not clear what the firm had been retained to do, the report said. The company has not commented beyond its statement announcing Huang's resignation. REPLACING HUANG Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. The New York Times also reported Wednesday that Huang had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him. While Kress offers investors a familiar hand after 13 years as CFO, analysts have pointed to Buck as a potential longer-term candidate because of Nvidia 's reliance on technical leadership. The veteran engineer helped develop its crucial CUDA software platform and now leads its hyperscale AI products. "The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap ... that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system," said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments. "In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself." Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.

TRUMP WEIGHS IN Trump said on Sunday that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country" and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy. On Thursday, the US president suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over as Nvidia 's CEO. US House Speaker Mike Johnson said it was "critically important for right successor to be chosen to replace Huang," noting there was a growing consensus in Congress on limiting exports of semiconductor chips to China. HUANG'S ROCK-STAR STATUS For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips' ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world's most valuable company. That turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. The scandal preceding Huang's departure unfolded over more than a year, beginning with an October 2025 New York Times report linking him to Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips. Subsequent reports said US intelligence officials believed Alice Huang was acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy. Washington has also investigated Megaspeed over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports.

Related:

Alice Huang barred from re-entering Singapore; insufficient evidence she committed offences in Megaspeed probe: MHA

What we know about Megaspeed, Singapore-based customer of Nvidia

Separately, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday that the US Justice Department was investigating Alice Huang over whether entities linked to her were involved in efforts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products to China, citing a person familiar with the matter. A spokesperson for the Manhattan US Attorney’s office declined to comment on the Bloomberg report. The office previously charged three people associated with Super Micro, including its co-founder, with helping smuggle at least US$2.5 billion of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws. Super Micro did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Earlier, the Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs said Singapore police had been investigating Super Micro as part of a wider probe into Megaspeed and Alice Huang. The police had reached out to the FBI and the Justice Department for help and had received "limited information or assistance," the ministry said. Earlier this month, Nvidia 's board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time. The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia 's vice president of healthcare, who reported to him.

Global AI-linked stocks tumbled on Thursday as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following a deepening scandal around his affairs, upending the chipmaker's leadership and posing fresh risks to a sector already reeling with funding and regulatory concerns. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said. As the centrepiece of the AI ecosystem, the chipmaker finances infrastructure built around its chips - a strategy that has drawn scrutiny over circular funding and now risks weighing on the sector as its crisis deepens. Nvidia's shares fell 8.2 per cent to a more than 16-month low in early trading and its market value was on track to close below US$4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.

"Nvidia has been called the 'Bank of AI'. If they have to take a step back because of what's going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That's an open question," said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading. Nvidia-backed neocloud firm CoreWeave dropped 9.1 per cent after surging more than 27 per cent in the previous session when its earnings ignited a relief rally in AI stocks. Other neocloud stocks, including IREN and Applied Digital, were also trading lower. Nebius dropped 16.2 per cent after the company said its 2026 revenue would come in at the low end of its previous forecast. Nvidia has lost more than US$550 billion in market value since the board announced an investigation on Sunday into Huang's relationship with a businesswoman called Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. "The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raises the question into whether that created more stability or more fragility. We're going to find out over the next few weeks as this whole situation unravels," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers. Nvidia short sellers have made US$9.6 billion in on-paper profits so far this week, according to data analytics firm ORTEX.

AI SELLOFF CONTINUES AFTER BRIEF RESPITE Chipmakers, widely viewed as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, led the selloff with the Philadelphia chips index sliding 1.3 per cent. Marvell Technology, which Huang called the "next trillion-dollar company" in June, slumped 3.8 per cent. AI hyperscaler Oracle, which is expanding its cloud AI chip deals with Nvidia, shed 2.6 per cent. Memory chipmaker Micron Technology fell 2.5 per cent and data storage firms Sandisk and Western Digital eased 6 per cent and 3.7 per cent. Photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent and AI server maker Dell eased between 3 per cent and 5.1 per cent. Construction and power-generation equipment maker Caterpillar and power producer Vistra slipped about 0.5 per cent each. Shares of AMD and Broadcom, which also produce AI chips and compete with Nvidia, however, rose 3.7 per cent and 5.6 per cent, respectively, on expectations that the turmoil at Nvidia could create opportunity for rivals. Other hyperscalers including Alphabet, Amazon.com and Microsoft were also up between 0.8 per cent and 2.7 per cent. AI stocks struggled and the Nasdaq entered a technical correction earlier this month after the Democrats swept the midterm elections, including in states opposed to data centres, stoking fears tighter regulation could slow the AI build-out. Tech-heavy stock markets across the globe witnessed jitters. Japan and South Korea closed nearly 0.7 per cent lower. Tech stocks in Europe were also down about 1 per cent. Nvidia trades at about 12 times its 12-month forward earnings estimates, its lowest since November 2012, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The Amsterdam-based company also raised its annual spending forecast, but said it would increasingly rely on customer prepayments and asset-backed financing rather than fresh capital to fund its expansion. The delays come as AI-linked stocks face pressure on several fronts, including financing concerns around neoclouds such as CoreWeave, uncertainty following the Democrats' US midterm election victory and Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO. Nebius said some third-party capacity expected to come online this year had been pushed back to the first half of 2027, though the contracts underpinning that capacity remained in place.

NEOCLOUDS BUCKLE UNDER NVIDIA SCARE Neoclouds including Nebius and CoreWeave are tied closely to Nvidia and Huang. The chip giant is heavily involved in the financing of both companies, being one of their most prominent backers. Analysts have warned that trouble at Nvidia could also result in volatility in neoclouds. Nebius raised its 2026 spending forecast to about $27 billion from the prior view of $20 billion to $25 billion, while next year's spending is expected to jump sharply to $40 billion to $45 billion. However, roughly 75 per cent to 85 per cent of the 2027 investments will be covered by prepayments from customers and asset-backed financing through existing contracts with hyperscalers such as Microsoft and Meta. Investors have been worried about AI demand after recent hyperscaler earnings hinted at a slower ramp in data-center spending. "We have no doubt that this capacity will be sold. Clients are looking for capacity already for 2028, and prices for 2027 are going up. We do not see any risk," Nebius CFO Dado Alonso said. Nebius' third-quarter revenue of $981 million beat estimates of $907.5 million. It expects 2026 revenue of $3 billion to $3.2 billion, trimming the higher end from $3.4 billion earlier. The ministry is hoping that NATO will recognise the centre, due to open in summer 2027, an official told reporters at a briefing.
